short: Timur captured an Ottoman sultan and left the Ottoman state to a decade of civil war.
full:
Bayezid I had spent a decade annexing the Turkmen beyliks of Anatolia and was besieging Constantinople when Timur invaded from the east. He broke off the siege and marched inland. Timur reached the Çubuk plain north-east of Ankara first, took the city's water supply and forced Bayezid to fight thirsty on ground of Timur's choosing on 20 July 1402. The dispossessed beylik contingents in the Ottoman line recognised their old lords in Timur's army and changed sides during the battle. The Serbian cavalry of Stefan Lazarevic fought well and withdrew; Bayezid was run down in flight and taken prisoner, the only Ottoman sultan ever captured, and died in captivity in March 1403.

Timur restored the beyliks, took tribute and went home to prepare his campaign against Ming China. Bayezid's sons fought each other for eleven years until Mehmed I reunified the state in 1413. The reprieve bought Constantinople another half-century, and the Ottoman advance into Europe resumed only after 1413.
